phrases.translation: Alif-Lãm-Ra. ˹This is˺ a Book whose verses are well perfected and then fully explained.
phrases.explanation: The separate letters open the chapter, and many early commentators left their exact meaning to Allah while treating them as part of revelation. The Book is then described as firmly constructed and later explained in detail, which joins strength of wording with clarity of judgment. A firmly built text does not collapse under questioning, and detailed explanation keeps its commands, stories, and promises from blurring into one another.

phrases.translation: ˹It is˺ from the One ˹Who is˺ All-Wise, All-Aware
phrases.explanation: The source named is the All Wise and All Aware, which answers in advance both the design and the knowledge of the Book. Wisdom governs what is said, while awareness covers the people addressed in their hidden and public states. The verse therefore introduces the Quran as speech measured by one who cannot be surprised by the excuses, griefs, and arguments that follow in the chapter.

phrases.translation: ˹Tell them, O Prophet,˺ “Worship none but Allah. Surely I am a warner and deliverer of good news to you from Him
phrases.explanation: Worship none but Allah gives the whole Book one centre before any story is related. The Prophet names his own role as warner and giver of good news from Him, so warning and welcome travel in the same voice. A warner without good news would crush, and good news without warning would flatter. Together they describe a messenger who protects people from danger while opening a better road.

phrases.translation: And seek your Lord’s forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance.
phrases.explanation: Seeking forgiveness and repenting come immediately after exclusive worship, because turning to Allah includes leaving the partners and habits that competed with Him. Forgiveness looks at past guilt, while repentance changes present direction. Put together at the opening, they tell a resistant audience that return is still available. The first demand of the chapter therefore carries an invitation inside it.

phrases.translation: He will grant you a good provision for an appointed term and graciously reward the doers of good.
phrases.explanation: Good provision for an appointed term promises that repentant people will be given wholesome enjoyment in this life until death, while every person of merit receives favour in a fuller measure. Early commentators linked the enjoyment with contentment, lawful provision, and a life not ruined by punishment. Worldly good is not mocked here. It is placed inside a term, after which a greater accounting begins.

phrases.translation: But if you turn away, then I truly fear for you the torment of a formidable Day
phrases.explanation: If they turn away, the Prophet fear for them introduces the torment of a great Day with pastoral concern rather than delight. Fear for you shows the warner carrying the danger of his audience in his own chest. A formidable Day gathers resurrection, judgment, and exposure into one appointment. Refusal is therefore not treated as a private taste, because the road after refusal has an end.

phrases.translation: To Allah is your return. And He is Most Capable of everything.”
phrases.explanation: To Allah is your return closes the opening summons with the destination behind every choice in the chapter. Most Capable of everything answers both denial of resurrection and confidence in worldly escape routes. The verse is brief because the argument needs a fixed point rather than another illustration. Worship, repentance, provision, and warning all make sense inside a life that is travelling back to its Maker.

phrases.translation: Indeed, they enfold ˹what is in˺ their hearts, ˹trying˺ to hide it from Him!
phrases.explanation: Folding their breasts pictures people curling inward to hide what is in their hearts from Allah, as early reports explained the image through turning away and covering themselves when revelation was recited. The body becomes a curtain for a secret. The attempted hiding is itself revealing, because innocence before God does not need to crouch. Their posture shows that they already sense an observer they wish to escape.

phrases.translation: But even when they cover themselves with their clothes, He knows what they conceal and what they reveal.
phrases.explanation: Garments pulled over the body cannot change the quality of divine knowledge. Clothes may hide a person from neighbours, weather, and shame, yet what is secret and what is public stand equal before Allah. The verse speaks to night behaviour and private gatherings as much as to a literal cloak. Security built on being unseen collapses once the unseen is understood as a human limit only.

phrases.translation: Surely He knows best what is ˹hidden˺ in the heart
phrases.explanation: He knows what is in the breasts makes the chest the true location of the story. Motives for denial, fear of exposure, and resentment toward the message are present before words form. This knowledge is warning for plotters and comfort for sincere people whose intentions are misread. The verse teaches that accountability reaches the first draft of an action, where many people still feel safely unpublished.

phrases.translation: There is no moving creature on earth whose provision is not guaranteed by Allah.
phrases.explanation: Every moving creature on earth has provision upon Allah, from insects under soil to birds crossing deserts and humans anxious over markets. The statement does not remove effort or seasons. It places the whole economy of eating inside divine care and knowledge. For a community hearing warnings about punishment, the verse also says that daily bread comes from a Lord who has not forgotten the smallest life.

phrases.translation: And He knows where it lives and where it is laid to rest.
phrases.explanation: He knows its dwelling and its resting place or repository, an expression early commentators connected with where a creature lives, where it dies, and stages before birth. Movement across earth never moves outside knowledge. A nest, burrow, womb, road, and grave are all addresses known in advance. The verse gives a quiet answer to fear of being lost inside a huge creation.

phrases.translation: All is ˹written˺ in a perfect Record
phrases.explanation: All in a clear Record joins provision to writing rather than improvisation. A record means no creature survives by accident outside the plan, and no act of human cruelty toward provision escapes the account. The same writing that comforts the hungry can rebuke hoarders and tyrants who block shares. Divine care is presented as exact, not as a vague feeling that the world usually works out.

phrases.translation: He is the One Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days—
phrases.explanation: Creation in six Days is stated with the measure left to Allah knowledge, the emphasis falling on ordered power rather than human calendaring. Heavens and earth arriving through stages show a Maker not hurried by need. The verse prepares for resurrection by grounding life in a power already displayed at a universal scale. A world that began by command can be returned by command.

phrases.translation: and His Throne was upon the waters—in order to test which of you is best in deeds.
phrases.explanation: His Throne was upon the water before the familiar order known to people, a statement early readers affirmed while exploring what water and priority meant. The purpose given is testing which people are best in deeds, using best rather than most to honour sincerity and excellence. Cosmic history therefore lands in the reader conduct today. Creation is not a museum piece but the arena of an examination still running.

phrases.translation: And if you ˹O Prophet˺ say, “Surely you will ˹all˺ be raised up after death,” the disbelievers will certainly say, “That is nothing but pure magic!”
phrases.explanation: If resurrection is announced, disbelievers call it clear magic, repeating the label used whenever power in speech unsettles settled expectations. Magic becomes a word for an effect they cannot deny feeling but refuse to attribute to God. The irony is sharp after a verse about the Maker of heavens and earth. A person can accept the body daily yet call its return impossible because habit has become theology.

phrases.translation: And if We delay their punishment until an appointed time, they will definitely say, “What is holding it back?”
phrases.explanation: Delay of punishment until a counted community or appointed time produces the question, what holds it back. The wording in early explanation points to a fixed period rather than hesitation in heaven. Mockers read mercy as weakness because their calendar measures truth by speed. The verse again exposes an audience that wants a date to argue with instead of a warning to obey.

phrases.translation: Indeed, on the Day it overtakes them, it will not be averted from them,
phrases.explanation: On the Day it reaches them nothing can turn it away, a change from postponement to certainty that leaves no manager for the event. Human delay has limits because the appointment was never under their lock. The sentence does not give the hour they demand. It gives the character of the hour, which is more useful for repentance than trivia about a schedule they cannot alter.

phrases.translation: and they will be overwhelmed by what they used to ridicule
phrases.explanation: What they mocked will surround them, turning a verbal joke into an environment. Mockery works while distance feels safe, since laughter creates a little room between speaker and consequence. Encirclement removes that room from every side. The verse uses their own object as the place they will stand, teaching that contempt can become a form of rehearsal for meeting what was laughed at.

phrases.translation: If We give people a taste of Our mercy then take it away from them, they become utterly desperate, ungrateful
phrases.explanation: A taste of mercy removed sends a type of person into despair and ingratitude, as if the loss proves that no good was ever real or will return. The chapter now studies emotional weather across changing fortune. Despair forgets the Giver during absence, while ingratitude erases the memory of the gift itself. Both failures make the self a poor historian, able to remember only the present temperature.

phrases.translation: But if We give them a taste of prosperity after being touched with adversity,
phrases.explanation: Prosperity after adversity produces the opposite forgetfulness in the same unstable person. Relief arrives, yet gratitude is replaced by boasting as if the new condition were a personal achievement and a permanent identity. The verse notices how quickly a sufferer can become an exhibitionist once the clinic, debt, danger, or hunger is behind him. Ease tests character by removing the pressure that once forced prayer.

phrases.translation: they say, “My ills are gone,” and become totally prideful and boastful
phrases.explanation: Evil has left me becomes a triumphant sentence that closes the file too quickly. Self exultation treats recovery as immunity and turns other sufferers into people supposedly less clever or worthy. In the moral pattern of the chapter, the healthy moment requires remembrance just as much as the painful moment required patience. Boasting is another form of heedlessness, only dressed in better clothes and a louder voice.

phrases.translation: except those who patiently endure and do good. It is they who will have forgiveness and a mighty reward
phrases.explanation: Those who are patient and do righteous deeds break the swing between despair and boasting. Patience steadies the heart when mercy seems withdrawn, while good works give prosperity somewhere useful to go when it returns. Forgiveness and a great reward answer this stability, because the believer is not owned by the last event. The verse offers a portrait of emotional worship, where fortune changes but direction does not.

phrases.translation: Perhaps you ˹O Prophet˺ may wish to give up some of what is revealed to you and may be distressed by it because they say,
phrases.explanation: Perhaps you might leave part of what is revealed addresses pressure felt by the Prophet when certain verses angered powerful hearers. The wording does not say he did omit revelation. It steadies him against the temptation every public teacher knows, namely softening the exact sentence that creates rejection. Distress in his chest is treated honestly, because carrying an unpopular message has an emotional cost even for a prophet.

phrases.translation: “If only a treasure had been sent down to him, or an angel had come with him!”
phrases.explanation: A treasure sent down or an angel walking beside him summarises the kind of credentials opponents would accept. Wealth would make leadership visible in their marketplace, while an angel would remove the scandal of an ordinary human messenger. Both requests ask heaven to dress truth in the costume of local status. The verse shows how an audience can discuss packaging for years to avoid the message inside it.

phrases.translation: You are only a warner, and Allah is the Trustee of All Affairs
phrases.explanation: You are only a warner returns the Prophet to his assigned office and relieves him of managing the universe of outcomes. Allah is trustee over all things, so provision, judgment, timing, and acceptance do not rest on prophetic anxiety. Limiting the role does not reduce its honour. It protects the messenger from editing revelation to create results that were never assigned to him.

phrases.translation: Or do they say, “He has fabricated this ˹Quran˺!”? Say, ˹O Prophet,
phrases.explanation: He fabricated it is quoted as the accusation behind many of the audience manoeuvres. Say turns the reply into a public challenge instead of a private defence of feelings. Fabrication implies a human workshop, sources, editing, and ambition, so the verse allows the accusers to use exactly those tools. A serious charge deserves a test that both sides can witness rather than another round of insinuation in gatherings.

phrases.translation: ˺ “Produce ten fabricated sûrahs like it and seek help from whoever you can—
phrases.explanation: Ten fabricated chapters like it gives them more than poetic fragments to produce, since the accusation claims a book length invention. Calling helpers besides Allah opens the contest to poets, soothsayers, scholars, allies, and any claimed unseen support. The scale matters because a short clever imitation might copy a mood. Ten chapters would need sustained guidance, law, story, argument, and spiritual force without the collapse expected from pretence.

phrases.translation: other than Allah—if what you say is true!”
phrases.explanation: If what you say is true ties the challenge to honesty about their own claim. Truthful accusers who truly believe a man produced the Quran should be able to marshall the best speech culture of Arabia toward a comparable work. Failure then becomes evidence rather than embarrassment alone. The verse respects their literary confidence enough to put it to work, making silence afterward speak in a language they understand.

phrases.translation: But if your helpers fail you, then know that it has been revealed with the knowledge of Allah,
phrases.explanation: If helpers do not answer, the conclusion commanded is that it was sent down with Allah knowledge. Knowledge here covers reports of the unseen, earlier history, future outcomes, and a coherence beyond the reciter unaided learning in the argument of the passage. Failed imitation alone does not create faith, yet it removes the fabrication theory that had protected denial. Evidence clears ground even when pride still refuses to walk.

phrases.translation: and that there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him!
phrases.explanation: No god except Him follows as the theological centre toward which the literary test was always pointing. A book that cannot be explained as human manufacture invites surrender to the God it names. The verse does not leave the audience admiring style from a distance. It asks what worship should look like once the source is recognised, because eloquence without obedience would become another way to delay.

phrases.translation: Will you ˹not˺ then submit ˹to Allah˺
phrases.explanation: Will you then submit asks for a decision after the excuse of fabrication has been tested. Submission in this context is the broad surrender to Allah that later becomes the name of the religion in practice. The question is gentler than a threat and more searching than applause. It exposes the final issue plainly, since many people can lose an argument and still postpone changing their lives.

phrases.translation: Whoever desires ˹only˺ this worldly life and its luxuries, We will pay them in full for their deeds in this life—nothing will be left out
phrases.explanation: Whoever wants only worldly life and its adornment is paid in full for deeds in that life, with nothing diminished from the visible return. Work can earn wealth, reputation, health, influence, or pleasure even when its intention never rises beyond earth. The verse does not call worldly effort useless. It warns that a person who asks only for the near wage may receive exactly the wage requested and discover its limit too late.

phrases.translation: It is they who will have nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire.
phrases.explanation: Nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire completes the bargain of those who wanted only worldly payment. A person can exhaust a life account in advance through fame, wealth, comfort, and applause, leaving no saved portion for the world where those currencies expire. The verse is severe because it takes their chosen goal seriously. They asked for the near life as the whole horizon, and the horizon closes.

phrases.translation: Their efforts in this life will be fruitless and their deeds will be useless
phrases.explanation: Fruitless effort and useless deeds in the ultimate sense means worldly results do not transfer as worship when Allah was never the aim. Buildings, victories, generosity for reputation, and clever work may remain visible in history while carrying no weight at judgment. The language protects pure intention rather than discouraging effort. A deed needs a destination beyond earth if it is to survive earth ending.

phrases.translation: ˹Can these people be compared to˺ those ˹believers˺ who stand on clear proof from their Lord,
phrases.explanation: A person on clear proof from his Lord is compared with the worldly seeker just described, a contrast early commentators applied to believers, the Prophet, and in some readings specific early followers. Clear proof means the heart is not guessing its direction. It stands on evidence strong enough to organise worship, patience, and hope. The unanswered comparison expects the reader to feel the inequality before trying to argue it.

phrases.translation: backed by ˹the Quran as˺ a witness from Him, and preceded by the Book of Moses ˹which was revealed˺ as a guide and mercy?
phrases.explanation: A witness from Him and the Book of Moses before it as guide and mercy place the Quran inside a chain of testimony. The witness was understood in several ways, including Gabriel, the Quran, or a confirming sign, and the passage keeps some of that openness in translation. Moses Book matters because continuity with earlier revelation makes denial harder to blame on novelty. Guidance and mercy also describe destination as well as history.

phrases.translation: It is those ˹believers˺ who have faith in it. But whoever from the ˹disbelieving˺ groups rejects it, the Fire will be their destiny.
phrases.explanation: Those who believe in it stand against parties who reject it and meet the Fire as promised place. Parties can include organised religious and political groups whose rejection becomes collective identity. Belief is not reduced to private agreement with a proof. It enters a side. The verse accepts social reality while insisting that numbers, ancestry, and party discipline cannot change the destination attached to refusal.

phrases.translation: So do not be in doubt of it. It is certainly the truth from your Lord, but most people do not believe
phrases.explanation: Do not be in doubt steadies the Prophet and every reader tempted to let majority rejection rewrite a clear conclusion. Truth from your Lord settles origin, while most people do not believe predicts the social weather around it. Certainty and loneliness can exist together for a long season. The verse teaches that a lonely truth is still truth, and a crowded falsehood still has to answer for its crowd.

phrases.translation: Who does more wrong than those who fabricate lies against Allah?
phrases.explanation: Who does more wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah returns to fabrication, now aimed at false claimants and those who assign partners, children, or rulings to God without knowledge. A lie at this altitude corrupts worship for everyone who receives it. It is ranked above ordinary falsehood because its victim list can grow across generations while wearing the costume of devotion.

phrases.translation: They will be brought before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, “These are the ones who lied against their Lord.”
phrases.explanation: Brought before their Lord places fabricators in a courtroom where witnesses identify them. Witnesses in early explanation include angels, prophets, and the records of deeds, voices that cannot be managed by the speakers who once controlled gatherings. These are the ones who lied gives public naming to words that had hidden behind sanctuaries and titles. Exposure is part of the sentence before punishment is even described.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah’s condemnation is upon the wrongdoers
phrases.explanation: The curse or condemnation of Allah upon wrongdoers means distance from mercy pronounced over a settled pattern. It is a judicial sound rather than a casual insult. Wrongdoers here are not merely people who made one inaccurate statement. They built authority around a lie about God and then defended the building. The verse ends with a title under which the next verse will list their public work.

phrases.translation: who hinder ˹others˺ from Allah’s Path, striving to make it ˹appear˺ crooked, and disbelieve in the Hereafter
phrases.explanation: Blocking others from the path and seeking to make it crooked describes fabrication in motion. A straight road can be made to look dangerous through mockery, selective quotation, intimidation, and elite pressure. Disbelief in the Hereafter removes the future court that might have restrained such campaigning. The verse joins private theology with public harm, because people who expect no meeting often treat other souls as traffic to control.

phrases.translation: They will never frustrate Allah on earth, and they will have no protector besides Allah.
phrases.explanation: They cannot frustrate Allah on earth and have no protectors besides Him, a sentence that removes both escape and sponsorship. Earthly influence may delay a messenger, frighten followers, or bend a road in public opinion, yet none of that binds God. Protector language answers the partner gods and tribal patrons trusted throughout the chapter. At judgment every supposed shield discovers it too needed shielding.

phrases.translation: Their punishment will be multiplied, for they failed to hear or see ˹the truth˺
phrases.explanation: Doubled punishment is connected with inability to hear or see in the moral sense developed across the passage. Ears and eyes were present while their use for truth was refused until refusal felt like incapacity. Early commentators also linked doubling with misleading others in addition to personal disbelief. Either way the multiplication follows layers of harm. A closed person who closes roads for others carries more than a private loss into judgment.

phrases.translation: It is they who have ruined themselves, and whatever ˹gods˺ they fabricated will fail them
phrases.explanation: They lost themselves gives the deepest account of the damage, because a soul can be spent while its owner still feels successful. Fabricated gods straying away completes the abandonment, as partners named in rituals are absent when their advertising is finally tested. Self loss and helper loss arrive together. The verse asks readers to watch an entire support system dissolve before deciding that worldly confidence is evidence of safety.

phrases.translation: Without a doubt, they will be the worst losers in the Hereafter
phrases.explanation: Greatest losers in the Hereafter is stated without doubt after the previous verse showed self and gods both gone. Loss is measured by exchange, because they traded guidance, time, conscience, and future mercy for temporary control of the road. Other losers may keep part of a fortune or reputation. These lose the self that could enjoy anything. The superlative belongs to an end where no asset survives transfer.

phrases.translation: Surely those who believe, do good, and humble themselves before their Lord will be the residents of Paradise. They will be there forever
phrases.explanation: Belief, righteous deeds, and humble quiet before their Lord describe the opposite company. The Arabic sense of humble settling suggests hearts that become still in obedience rather than constantly bargaining with commands. Residents of Paradise forever gives that stillness a home where it will no longer be interrupted by grief or fatigue. The verse balances the greatest losers with people whose lowliness became the path into permanence.

phrases.translation: The example of these two parties is that of the blind and the deaf, compared to the seeing and the hearing.
phrases.explanation: Blind and deaf beside seeing and hearing condenses the two parties into faculties. The comparison is about reception of truth, not insult toward people with physical disabilities. One party lives in a world where signs make no sound and evidences cast no light, while the other uses the same world as a speaking place. The verse follows ears and eyes being misused, giving the reader a simple test of spiritual function.

phrases.translation: Can the two be equal? Will you not then be mindful
phrases.explanation: Can the two be equal and will you not remember asks the audience to complete an obvious judgment. Equality cannot be rescued by calling both groups sincere in their own tradition when one can receive proof and the other blocks it. Remembrance is the intended result because the comparison should awaken a person before seals harden. A parable can succeed where a long argument failed by making the difference visible at once.

phrases.translation: Surely We sent Noah to his people. ˹He said,˺ “Indeed, I am sent to you with a clear warning
phrases.explanation: Noah is introduced as a clear warner, beginning a long sequence of prophetic stories that will test the opening claims of the chapter. Clarity matters because later rejection cannot hide behind confusion about his office. The first audience of Muhammad hears its own situation in an ancient town. A man stands among his people with no army, treasure, or angel beside him, only a warning whose clarity becomes the offence.

phrases.translation: that you should worship none but Allah. I truly fear for you the torment of a painful Day.”
phrases.explanation: Worship none but Allah gives Noah warning the same centre as the opening of the chapter, proving that the demand did not begin with Muhammad. I fear for you the punishment of a painful Day joins affection with alarm. A warner who fears for people is not enjoying their danger. He sees a destination their habits have hidden, and love takes the form of saying so before weather changes.

phrases.translation: The disbelieving chiefs of his people said, “We see you only as a human being like ourselves,
phrases.explanation: The chiefs answer by reducing Noah to a mere human like themselves. Equality in body is treated as disqualification, although his difference lies in revelation rather than anatomy. Elites often prefer a supernatural messenger because an ordinary neighbour carrying God word disturbs the local ranking of importance. Their first sentence discusses the vessel so the cargo can be left unopened for a little longer.

phrases.translation: and we see that no one follows you except the lowliest among us, who do so ˹hastily˺ without thinking.
phrases.explanation: Lowliest followers who joined at first glance turns social contempt into evidence. Poor and socially weak believers are accused of following without thought, although they may simply have less invested in the old order. The chiefs read speed as shallowness when people beneath them decide quickly. In the story of many prophets, early faith among the marginal becomes one of the clearest signs that status, not proof, is governing rejection.

phrases.translation: We do not see anything that makes ˹all of˺ you any better than us.
phrases.explanation: We see no superiority of you over us shifts the issue from truth to rank. If Noah and his followers cannot display wealth, learning, birth, or force above the council, the council feels entitled to dismiss them. The verse exposes a scale on which revelation must arrive already seated at the top table. A message carried by ordinary people threatens that scale more than it threatens their theology.

phrases.translation: In fact, we think you are liars.”
phrases.explanation: We think you are liars finishes the progression from humanity, followers, and rank to character assassination. Think sounds cautious, yet it licenses total rejection without producing a counter argument. Labelling a whole small community liars protects the chiefs from interviewing converted neighbours honestly. The verse allows the reader to watch prejudice assemble itself into a verdict while calling the process reasonable.

phrases.translation: He said, “O my people! Consider if I stand on a clear proof from my Lord and He has blessed me with a mercy from Himself, which you fail to see.
phrases.explanation: Noah asks them to consider the possibility that he stands on clear proof and a mercy from his Lord which has been obscured to them. Mercy can refer to prophethood itself, and obscured suggests that a gift can be present while pride prevents sight. His question is invitational rather than triumphant. He grants their experience of not seeing while refusing to let that experience become final evidence that nothing is there.

phrases.translation: Should we ˹then˺ force it on you against your will
phrases.explanation: Shall we compel you to accept it while you dislike it establishes a principle inside prophetic preaching. Hidden mercy cannot be forced into a heart by pressure from Noah, and public surrender under compulsion would not be seeing. The sentence also protects the poor followers from being treated as proof of manipulation. Faith has arrived by recognition among some and remains resisted by others, a difference no council can settle by etiquette.

phrases.translation: O my people! I do not ask you for a payment for this ˹message˺.
phrases.explanation: No payment asked for the message removes income from Noah motives and answers the charge of seeking superiority. A preacher building status often needs wealthy patrons and fees, yet Noah declares complete independence from their purse. That freedom allows him to welcome poor believers without calculating their public value. The verse makes economics reveal theology, because the source of a wage often decides whose feelings will be protected.

phrases.translation: My reward is only from Allah. And I will never dismiss the believers, for they will surely meet their Lord.
phrases.explanation: My reward is with Allah explains why he will not drive away believers to make the council comfortable. Those believers will meet their Lord, so their worth is set in a court far above social embarrassment. A messenger paid by God does not need to sell access to elites. His refusal becomes a defence of human dignity inside the preaching task, especially where poverty is treated as contamination.

phrases.translation: But I can see that you are a people acting ignorantly
phrases.explanation: You are a people who act ignorantly is direct but still diagnostic. Ignorance here means judging a divine message by birth, wealth, and the seating order of a town. Calling it ignorance rather than simple evil leaves a door for education while refusing to flatter the standard. Noah will not pretend their scale is sophisticated just because it belongs to chiefs. Sometimes clarity is the first mercy offered to arrogance.

phrases.translation: O my people! Who would protect me from Allah if I were to dismiss them? Will you not then be mindful
phrases.explanation: Who would help me against Allah if I drove them away makes exclusion of poor believers a sin with consequences for the prophet himself. Noah imagines standing before God after trading sincere followers for elite approval and finding no defender. That fear protects the marginal better than public sympathy would. Will you not remember asks the council to notice that God court does not use their guest list.

phrases.translation: I do not say to you that I possess Allah’s treasuries or know the unseen,
phrases.explanation: Noah does not claim Allah treasuries or knowledge of the unseen, directly cancelling the qualifications his opponents demand from a messenger. He has no storehouse from which to purchase followers and no private access to every future event. Such limits are part of honest prophethood. A person inventing authority to win elites might promise wealth and secrets, yet Noah gives up both bargaining chips before discussion begins.

phrases.translation: nor do I claim to be an angel, nor do I say that Allah will never grant goodness to those you look down upon.
phrases.explanation: Nor am I an angel and nor do I say to the despised believers that Allah will give them no good joins two refusals. He will not pretend to a different nature, and he will not pronounce hopelessness over people whose poverty offends the council. The eyes that look down are named gently, because the disease sits in the look. Heaven may be preparing good for a person the town cannot imagine honouring.

phrases.translation: Allah knows best what is ˹hidden˺ within them. ˹If I did,˺ then I would truly be one of the wrongdoers.”
phrases.explanation: Allah knows best what is in their souls protects poor believers from public psychoanalysis. If Noah condemned them without knowledge he would become a wrongdoer, a self warning that gives his tenderness moral force. Leadership is shown refusing a cruel verdict demanded by important people. The verse ends with the prophet placing his own possible sin in view rather than hiding behind office.

phrases.translation: They protested, “O Noah! You have argued with us far too much,
phrases.explanation: You have argued with us and prolonged argument records the fatigue of a council that has heard centuries of preaching in the wider story. Repetition has become their complaint because each new warning reminds them of an old refusal. People may call a message excessive simply because conscience will not let them forget it. The verse lets impatience confess how long mercy has been knocking.

phrases.translation: so bring upon us what you threaten us with, if what you say is true.”
phrases.explanation: Bring what you promise if you are truthful turns exhaustion into a dare. They demand punishment as a shortcut out of conversation, much like the later audiences in the chapter. A threat treated as a scheduling problem can be mocked until the day it becomes weather. The dare also reveals their confidence that a mere man cannot deliver what he announces, which is why Noah answer immediately returns agency to Allah.

phrases.translation: He responded, “It is Allah Who can bring it upon you if He wills, and then you will have no escape
phrases.explanation: Allah brings it if He wills takes the dare out of Noah hands and places timing where it belongs. The messenger announces a real danger without owning its calendar or mechanism. You cannot frustrate Him means their current safety is not an escape route already discovered. The sentence makes delay feel different, because unarrived punishment is now suspended by will rather than blocked by human strength.

phrases.translation: My advice will not benefit you—no matter how hard I try—if Allah wills ˹for˺ you to stray.
phrases.explanation: My sincere counsel will not benefit you if Allah wills to leave you astray is a painful sentence from a preacher who still wants to advise well. Early interpretation located the will in response to persistent rejection rather than arbitrary diversion at the first hearing. Counsel needs a receptive soil, and Noah admits he cannot manufacture it. His love reaches its limit at the boundary of another person surrender.

phrases.translation: He is your Lord, and to Him you will ˹all˺ be returned.”
phrases.explanation: He is your Lord and to Him you return gathers even rebels under a lordship they deny in practice. Return gives the long argument a destination beyond the town council and the unfinished Ark. Noah can stop measuring his worth by their response once the record is safely with God. The verse also reminds opponents that rejecting a messenger does not remove them from the messenger Lord jurisdiction.

phrases.translation: Or do they say, “He has fabricated this ˹Quran˺!”? Say, ˹O Prophet,
phrases.explanation: Or do they say he fabricated it interrupts Noah story to address Muhammad accusation in the present. Say makes the answer a public separation of responsibility rather than a debate about literary style after the earlier challenge. Similar charges travel across centuries because invention is easier to allege than repentance is to practise. The verse teaches the Prophet to answer cleanly without absorbing the guilt invented by opponents.

phrases.translation: ˺ “If I have done so, then I bear the burden of that sin!
phrases.explanation: If I fabricated it then my crime is upon me accepts the hypothetical penalty with complete clarity. No innocent messenger needs to blur the account or share blame with followers. The confidence of the sentence lies in its conditional form, because only a person certain of the source can state the consequence so plainly. It also puts every religious claim under personal responsibility before God.

phrases.translation: But I am free from your sinful accusation.”
phrases.explanation: I am innocent of what you commit completes the separation, including their false accusation and the denial built around it. Innocence does not mean indifference, since preaching continues after this verse. It means the Prophet will not carry an invented sin in his record merely because a crowd named it. Each party leaves the exchange holding its own work, which is the only honest way for judgment to begin.

phrases.translation: And it was revealed to Noah, “None of your people will believe except those who already have.
phrases.explanation: Revelation tells Noah that no more of his people will believe beyond those who already have, closing a mission whose length lay hidden inside the town mockery. Such knowledge belongs to Allah rather than pastoral exhaustion, and it changes Noah task from persuasion to preparation. The sentence can sound crushing, yet it releases him from endlessly trying new tones for hearts whose outcome God has disclosed.

phrases.translation: So do not be distressed by what they have been doing
phrases.explanation: Do not grieve over what they used to do cares for the prophet emotions at the moment of closure. Grief might have become self blame after generations of work ended with a small company. Divine speech names their actions as the cause, not a failure in his sincerity. A messenger may need comfort as much as instruction when a door closes, and this comfort protects the next act of obedience from bitterness.

phrases.translation: And build the Ark under Our ˹watchful˺ Eyes and directions, and do not plead with Me for those who have done wrong, for they will surely be drowned.”
phrases.explanation: Build the Ark under Our eyes and revelation turns carpentry into supervised obedience. Divine eyes here convey care, knowledge, and protection in classical explanation, so Noah works watched by the Lord laughed at by passersby. Do not plead for wrongdoers closes intercession for people whose end has been decreed through persistent injustice. The same command that starts rescue also teaches Noah the painful limits prayer will soon meet inside his own family.

phrases.translation: So he began to build the Ark, and whenever some of the chiefs of his people passed by, they mocked him.
phrases.explanation: Chiefs passing and mocking the Ark gives the work a public gallery. A boat built away from any floodwater they could see became a travelling joke for men of status with time to stop. Their laughter assumes the sky has finished speaking because the ground remains dry. Noah keeps building under a different report, which makes patience visible in timber long before it becomes rescue.

phrases.translation: He said, “If you laugh at us, we will ˹soon˺ laugh at you similarly
phrases.explanation: If you mock us we mock you as you mock should be read as a solemn reciprocal warning rather than schoolyard delight. A future reversal will expose whose work was absurd on the day water judges both ship and street. Noah does not stop to win the joke contest with every passing group. He names the coming reversal and returns to building, allowing time rather than repartee to finish the argument.

phrases.translation: You will soon come to know who will be visited by a humiliating torment ˹in this life˺ and overwhelmed by an everlasting punishment ˹in the next˺.”
phrases.explanation: You will know who receives a humiliating punishment and on whom lasting punishment settles distinguishes worldly disgrace from the next world permanence. The flood will answer in history, yet judgment continues after the historical water recedes. Knowledge delayed is still knowledge when the event arrives. Noah sentence gives mockers one final form of education, namely experience, while quietly warning present readers to learn by a cheaper method.

phrases.translation: And when Our command came and the oven burst ˹with water˺,
phrases.explanation: When Our command came and the oven gushed marks the sign through a domestic object turned into a fountain. Early commentators differed over the oven and its location, with some taking the word for the surface of the earth or a known baking oven whose water announced the flood. Preserve that detail with modesty. The shared point is unmistakable, because an ordinary marker tells Noah the awaited moment has opened.

phrases.translation: We said ˹to Noah˺, “Take into the Ark a pair from every species along with your family—
phrases.explanation: Carry pairs of every kind gathers animal life into the rescue under human responsibility. Pairs suggest continuity after judgment, since the Ark is a seed vessel for a renewed world rather than only a lifeboat for spectators. Along with family, the command shapes a small ordered society inside the coming chaos. Preservation is presented as work Allah assigns, not as a miracle that removes the need to load, count, and care.

phrases.translation: except those against whom the decree ˹to drown˺ has already been passed—and those who believe.”
phrases.explanation: Except those against whom the word has already gone forth places a boundary inside the family command before the son scene makes it personal. Blood relationship alone does not pull a person through the door of the Ark. Those who believe are added as the true company, widening family by faith while narrowing it by rejection. The verse is preparing a painful redefinition that Noah will need heaven to teach him.

phrases.translation: But none believed with him except for a few
phrases.explanation: Only a few believed with him measures centuries of preaching without exaggerating the harvest. Small numbers can feel like failure to a town and like faithfulness to heaven at the same time. The saved company is still enough to carry worship, memory, animals, and humanity into the next age. Scripture repeatedly resists the idea that truth can be weighed with a census taken before the storm.

phrases.translation: And he said, “Board it! In the Name of Allah it will sail and cast anchor.
phrases.explanation: Board it, in the name of Allah be its sailing and its anchoring, turns embarkation into worship. The name is spoken over departure and arrival, the two moments sailors cannot fully control even in calm weather. A wooden vessel becomes a lesson in dependence when its captain confesses that movement and rest both belong to God. The phrase has since become a natural prayer for journeys because it is exact and brief.

phrases.translation: Surely my Lord is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.”
phrases.explanation: My Lord is Forgiving and Merciful explains the tone aboard the Ark amid judgment. Rescue is not presented as a medal for flawless people since the few aboard still travel under pardon and mercy. Forgiveness looks backward at need, while mercy holds the vessel through water ahead. Beginning the voyage with those names keeps survivors from turning survival into arrogance while waves prepare to erase a world behind them.

phrases.translation: And ˹so˺ the Ark sailed with them through waves like mountains.
phrases.explanation: Sailing through waves like mountains lifts the Ark scene beyond a river crossing into a landscape made of moving water. Mountains usually mean stability, so making waves mountain sized gives terror a shape the eye can measure. The vessel remains small inside a rewritten geography. Only after that scale is set does the story narrow to a father voice calling across the noise.

phrases.translation: Noah called out to his son, who stood apart, “O my dear son!
phrases.explanation: Noah calls his son who stands apart, and the physical distance matches a spiritual separation already chosen. My son carries tenderness to the last possible moment, because prophetic duty has not dried a father heart. Apart may describe a separate place on rising ground, yet in the story it also describes a lifetime position toward the message. The call therefore contains years of hope compressed into one public shout.

phrases.translation: Come aboard with us and do not be with the disbelievers.”
phrases.explanation: Come aboard with us and do not be with the disbelievers gives the son two companies rather than a lecture. The Ark is near enough to board if pride can move faster than water. Noah names the other side plainly because vague kindness would waste the remaining seconds. Every parent of a wandering child can recognise the urgency, although the judgment scale here gives it an unbearable sharpness.

phrases.translation: He replied, “I will take refuge on a mountain, which will protect me from the water.”
phrases.explanation: A mountain will protect me answers a flood sent by God with altitude and self rescue. The son trusts the most solid feature in ordinary geography while refusing the vessel prepared through revelation. His plan is not physically silly in a normal rainstorm, which is why it reveals a deeper error. He treats a divine decree as weather that can be managed by choosing better ground.

phrases.translation: Noah cried, “Today no one is protected from Allah’s decree except those to whom He shows mercy!”
phrases.explanation: No protector today from Allah command except those He mercies corrects the category of the event. This is not a contest between boat and mountain technology. It is a judgment in which every refuge works only by mercy. Noah words also defend the Ark, since wood is no stronger than rock unless God makes it the appointed means. Faith trusts the appointed mercy rather than admiring its own equipment.

phrases.translation: And the waves came between them, and his son was among the drowned
phrases.explanation: The wave comes between them and the son is among the drowned ends the conversation without a farewell speech. Water interrupts sight before it ends life, so separation happens first as a wall across a father view. The brevity is devastating because no extra moral commentary is added in the verse. A hand stretched toward the reader is left in the air, and the story trusts silence to carry the wound.

phrases.translation: And it was said, “O earth! Swallow up your water.
phrases.explanation: O earth swallow your water addresses the ground as a servant that can receive back what rose from springs and soil. The flood begins to end by command, not by exhausted weather losing interest. Creation listens in pieces, each element assigned its part in judgment and then in restoration. A world unmade by water can be folded back toward habitability when the same voice that released it gives the reverse order.

phrases.translation: And O sky! Withhold ˹your rain˺.” The floodwater receded and the decree was carried out.
phrases.explanation: O sky hold back, the water subsided, and the matter was accomplished gathers the ending with administrative calm. Rain stops, levels fall, and a decree long announced becomes completed history. Accomplished deserves attention because it prevents the flood from feeling like uncontrolled destruction. Heaven and earth return to order under instruction, while human beings are left to read a changed landscape and understand why the old one vanished.

phrases.translation: The Ark rested on Mount Judi, and it was said, “Away with the wrongdoing people!”
phrases.explanation: The Ark rests on al Judi, a mountain whose location received traditional discussion, and the sentence away with the wrongdoing people sounds over the emptied world. Rest gives the vessel a Sabbath like stillness after mountain waves. Away can mean distance from mercy and perishing from the land at once. The first sound on dry ground is therefore not celebration alone, but judgment remembered beside survival.

phrases.translation: Noah called out to his Lord, saying, “My Lord! Certainly my son is ˹also˺ of my family,
phrases.explanation: Noah calls his Lord after the rescue and says my son is of my family, appealing to a relationship no decree has erased from a father heart. His argument begins with belonging rather than accusation. The earlier exception now hurts in a specific face, and Noah brings the tension to God instead of carrying silent resentment onto dry land. Prayer becomes a place where prophetic grief can speak honestly.

phrases.translation: Your promise is surely true, and You are the most just of all judges!”
phrases.explanation: Your promise is true and You are the wisest or most just of judges frames the question inside trust. Noah does not accuse heaven of breaking faith even while he cannot yet reconcile family, promise, and drowning. Supreme judge can also carry the sense of final decision maker whose knowledge exceeds a parent reading by blood. The verse models complaint that remains worship, because pain is carried upward rather than made into a rival theology.

phrases.translation: Allah replied, “O Noah! He is certainly not of your family—he was entirely of unrighteous conduct.
phrases.explanation: He is not of your family redefines household by righteous belonging rather than denying that the drowned young man was Noah offspring in ordinary speech. Early commentators discussed family here as the people promised rescue, namely the household of faith. Unrighteous conduct places his chosen life at the centre. The reply is painful because it tells a father that a category he loves cannot overrule judgment based on truth.

phrases.translation: So do not ask Me about what you have no knowledge of!
phrases.explanation: Do not ask Me about what you have no knowledge of corrects the request hidden inside Noah appeal. He knew the boy as son, but he did not know all that made the exception necessary. Prayer can cross a boundary when love asks God to act against a disclosed justice. The command draws a line around intercession without shaming the grief that brought the question into the open.

phrases.translation: I warn you so you do not fall into ignorance.”
phrases.explanation: I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant frames correction as revelation offered to a prophet for his protection. Ignorance here would mean speaking into a divine matter from a partial family map. Even Noah needs knowledge from above at the border between mercy and judgment. The gentleness sits in timing, because heaven teaches the beloved servant before grief hardens into a false conclusion about the promise.

phrases.translation: Noah pleaded, “My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You about what I have no knowledge of,
phrases.explanation: I seek refuge in You from asking what I do not know turns Noah pain into immediate surrender. Refuge is taken with the same Lord whose answer wounded him, a pattern already seen in the chapter picture of safety. He does not defend the wording of his appeal or negotiate a softer category. Correction accepted quickly becomes worship, especially when the corrected person could have used seniority and suffering as excuses.

phrases.translation: and unless You forgive me and have mercy on me, I will be one of the losers.”
phrases.explanation: Unless You forgive me and have mercy on me I will be among the losers places Noah inside the human need his preaching announced to others. A prophet who survived a world flood still asks not to lose himself through one ignorant request. Losers here are people whose account finally empties, using the chapter commercial language. The prayer teaches that rescue from water is not the only rescue a soul needs.

phrases.translation: It was said, “O Noah! Disembark with Our peace and blessings on you and some of the descendants of those with you.
phrases.explanation: Disembark with peace from Us and blessings gives Noah a new beginning guarded by the same Lord who corrected him. Peace answers water, grief, and social extinction with safety, while blessings look toward descendants and provision beyond the passengers. Some of those with him will carry families into nations, so dry land is not an epilogue. It is an examination ground rebuilt after judgment, still needing righteous conduct.

phrases.translation: As for the others, We will allow them ˹a brief˺ enjoyment, then they will be touched with a painful punishment from Us.”
phrases.explanation: Other communities will enjoy for a while and then painful punishment will touch them looks beyond the first happy landing into future generations from the saved company. Survival does not vaccinate descendants against denial, as the rest of the chapter will show through Ad, Thamud, and others. For a while keeps worldly success in its small frame. The new world starts with a warning written into the blessing.

phrases.translation: This is one of the stories of the unseen, which we reveal to you ˹O Prophet˺.
phrases.explanation: These are reports of the unseen revealed to Muhammad, giving the Noah account a source beyond local storytelling. Details such as private prayer after the flood locate the knowledge in revelation rather than public archive. The verse steps out of the ancient scene and addresses the new messenger directly. A story is therefore both history and credentials, because the man reciting it had no ordinary route to this interior record.

phrases.translation: Neither you nor your people knew it before this. So be patient!
phrases.explanation: Neither you nor your people knew it before this strengthens the claim from public ignorance as well as personal biography. A shared folk memory cannot easily explain the specific exchange about Noah son in this form. So be patient turns credential into instruction, since knowing a prophet story in detail is meant to teach the current prophet how to remain in his own long season without surrendering to mockery.

phrases.translation: Surely the ultimate outcome belongs ˹only˺ to the righteous
phrases.explanation: The outcome belongs to the God fearing gives patience a destination rather than a mood. Outcome can include vindication in history and the final world where every story settles. Noah did not control the middle of his story, yet righteousness and trust reached dry land. Muhammad is asked to measure his work by the same horizon. The verse makes the end of one prophet into fuel for another.

phrases.translation: And to the people of ’Âd We sent their brother Hûd.
phrases.explanation: To Ad their brother Hud repeats the pattern of a messenger known by kinship rather than imported from a foreign court. Brother signals shared lineage, language, and social trust that make rejection more painful and less excusable. Ad were remembered in early reports for size, strength, and impressive building in southern Arabia. Their story begins with nearness, so their coming arrogance cannot be blamed on a stranger accent.

phrases.translation: He said, “O my people! Worship Allah. You have no god other than Him.
phrases.explanation: Worship Allah, you have no god other than Him uses the same centre Noah announced, joining nations across centuries under one prophetic sentence. A new setting does not require a new ultimate loyalty. The directness is part of the mercy because Ad energy and architecture had grown around false objects. Hud asks them to move the centre before asking them to rearrange lesser habits.

phrases.translation: You do nothing but fabricate lies ˹against Allah˺
phrases.explanation: You only fabricate names the invention underneath their gods and claims. Fabrication can sound artistic when statues, myths, and priestly authorities make it beautiful, yet the word brings it back to a workshop. What human beings invent cannot give them orders from heaven simply because a generation forgets the invention date. Hud challenges the calendar by which a made thing becomes untouchable.

phrases.translation: O my people! I do not ask you for any reward for this ˹message˺.
phrases.explanation: No wage asked by Hud separates his call from the material interests of Ad elite culture. A strong people might suspect that a preacher wants position within their building economy or protection from their clan. He closes that market immediately. Free speech in the deepest sense appears here, because no salary can be withdrawn to make the message soften at the exact point where power feels judged.

phrases.translation: My reward is only from the One Who created me. Will you not then understand
phrases.explanation: My reward is with the One who created me gives his independence a source more intimate than public salary. Creator language is fitting for people proud of bodies and constructions, since the Maker of the messenger also made every builder listening. Will you not reason asks them to connect payment, motive, creation, and worship with ordinary intelligence. The evidence they need begins inside their own origin.

phrases.translation: And O my people! Seek your Lord’s forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance.
phrases.explanation: Seek forgiveness and repent repeats the opening invitation of the chapter inside Ad story, making structural echoes part of the teaching. A nation famous for power still begins recovery by admitting guilt, not by building higher. Forgiveness is asked from the Lord they displaced with fabricated gods. Repentance would turn national strength toward gratitude instead of letting it mature into a larger instrument of denial.

phrases.translation: He will shower you with rain in abundance, and add strength to your strength.
phrases.explanation: He will send the sky upon you in showers and add strength to your strength joins rain with social power in the promise. Early explanation pictured abundant rain restoring crops and children, while added strength preserves the good they already prize under new obedience. Repentance is not described as national shrinkage. Properly directed power can increase when its source is acknowledged, because blessing no longer has to feed arrogance in secret.

phrases.translation: So do not turn away, persisting in wickedness.”
phrases.explanation: Do not turn away as guilty people ends with direction and legal identity together. Turning away after forgiveness, rain, and strength have been offered becomes more than a change in taste. It is persistence in a crime against the Giver. Hud alternatives are vivid enough that later destruction cannot be read as a trap. A wet, strong, forgiven future stood beside the dry ruin they chose.

phrases.translation: They argued, “O Hûd! You have not given us any clear proof,
phrases.explanation: You have not brought clear proof repeats the demand pattern even after preaching, character, and warning have been placed before them. Clear proof for Ad may mean a sign they can classify without surrendering their gods, a standard designed to fail. Their sentence does not identify what evidence would count. That omission matters, because a moving target can keep rejection looking reasonable long after every reasonable request has been answered.

phrases.translation: and we will never abandon our gods upon your word, nor will we believe in you
phrases.explanation: We will not abandon our gods for your word and we are not believers in you states the actual decision beneath the evidence talk. The issue becomes loyalty to inherited objects rather than shortage of information. Your word diminishes revelation into personal opinion so the council can compare speakers. The verse teaches readers to listen for the point where requests for proof become protective language around an already chosen no.

phrases.translation: All we can say is that some of our gods have possessed you with evil.”
phrases.explanation: Some of our gods have struck you with evil explains Hud persistence as madness caused by offended deities. Mental illness language is used socially here to quarantine a critic, much as magic labels function elsewhere. If the speaker can be diagnosed by his opponents, his sentences no longer require answers. The accusation also gives their statues a power they had not demonstrated, imagined mainly to explain why a sane kinsman would defy the town.

phrases.translation: He said, “I call Allah to witness, and you too bear witness, that I ˹totally˺ reject whatever you associate
phrases.explanation: Hud calls Allah and the audience to witness his innocence from what they associate. Public dissociation is the opposite of the confusion they attribute to him, because his loyalty is singular and coherent. Bear witness makes the declaration a document they cannot later soften into negotiation. In a culture where gods were woven into clan protection, innocence from partners sounds like social nakedness. Hud accepts that exposure as the price of truth.

phrases.translation: with Him ˹in worship˺. So let all of you plot against me without delay
phrases.explanation: Plot against me all together without delay continues a Noah like challenge from a man with no visible army. He invites the whole coalition and its gods to stop using diagnosis as delay. Such speech is not recklessness for applause. It withdraws the leverage of gradual intimidation by placing his life inside a trust the next verse will name. One person can sound unshakeable when numbers have stopped being his evidence.

phrases.translation: I have put my trust in Allah—my Lord and your Lord.
phrases.explanation: I have trusted Allah, my Lord and your Lord, places opponents under the same sovereignty even while they threaten him. Your Lord denies them the comfort of a separate jurisdiction guarded by local gods. Trust follows the challenge rather than preceding it in the sentence order the translation gives, making the ground of courage visible. Hud does not need to outnumber Ad because the Lord of Ad already governs their next breath.

phrases.translation: There is no living creature that is not completely under His control.
phrases.explanation: No creature moves without its forelock in His grasp turns complete control into a physical image of a head held by the front hair. People, animals, armies, and plotters all travel inside a hold they cannot slip. The forelock suggests direction as well as power, since a creature is led where its head is turned. Hud safety rests on the grip that includes his enemies, not on escaping their geography.

phrases.translation: Surely my Lord’s Way is perfect justice
phrases.explanation: My Lord is on a straight path assures hearers that total control is not arbitrary cruelty. Straightness here conveys justice, truth, and right management in early explanation. The God who holds every forelock does not wander between moods or lose the innocent inside the guilty crowd. Trust becomes rational inside the story because power and moral straightness occupy the same hand, unlike the crooked path opponents try to make inviting.

phrases.translation: But if you turn away, I have already delivered to you what I have been sent with.
phrases.explanation: If you turn away I have conveyed what I was sent with closes Hud responsibility without closing his compassion too early. Delivery can be complete even when acceptance is absent, a distinction every prophet in the chapter needs. He will not chase the audience into editing the message just to record a response. The sentence gives preachers a boundary at which effort remains honourable although the town remains unmoved.

phrases.translation: My Lord will replace you with others. You are not harming Him in the least.
phrases.explanation: My Lord will replace you with another people and you will not harm Him removes national indispensability. Ad strength, buildings, and numbers cannot make heaven dependent on their survival. Replacement is a historical warning as much as a theological one, since land can receive new inhabitants after a proud civilisation falls. Their rejection injures their own future while the Lord remains exactly where He was.

phrases.translation: Indeed, my Lord is a ˹vigilant˺ Keeper over all things.”
phrases.explanation: My Lord is guardian over all things ends the speech with watchful preservation rather than a parting insult. Guardian language covers the threatened prophet, the plotting chiefs, and every creature whose forelock was just mentioned. Nothing in the confrontation slips into a private zone outside observation. Hud can walk away from the council because the real custody of events has never belonged to the room.

phrases.translation: When Our command came, We rescued Hûd and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us, saving them from a harsh torment
phrases.explanation: When Our command came, Hud and believers were saved by mercy from a harsh punishment. The wind that destroyed Ad in wider Quranic telling is compressed here into command and rescue, keeping attention on separation rather than spectacle. Mercy names their survival as gift, not a natural result of being on the right side of the weather. Harsh punishment also lets the reader feel why escape mattered without slowing into physical detail.

phrases.translation: That was ’Âd. They denied the signs of their Lord, disobeyed His messengers, and followed the command of every stubborn tyrant
phrases.explanation: That was Ad points to a finished civilisation as if to ruins on a road. They denied their Lord signs, disobeyed His messengers in the pattern represented by Hud, and followed every stubborn tyrant among their leaders. National failure is therefore political as well as theological. A people can be physically impressive while its chain of command leads eyes away from every sign. Strength became the vehicle, not the excuse, for ruin.

phrases.translation: They were followed by a curse in this world, as they will be on the Day of Judgment.
phrases.explanation: A curse followed them in this world and on the Day of Resurrection gives Ad a travelling sentence that outlives the wind. In history their name becomes warning, while in the next world distance from mercy becomes personal. The double horizon prevents ruins from being only an archaeological event. Memory itself can carry judgment when a civilisation name teaches later travellers what unrepentant power earns.

phrases.translation: Surely ’Âd denied their Lord. So away with ’Âd, the people of Hûd
phrases.explanation: Surely Ad disbelieved in their Lord and away with Ad, the people of Hud, closes with the same away sounded after the flood. Repetition links water and wind under one moral grammar. Naming them people of Hud preserves the rejected relationship inside the epitaph, because they will be remembered by the brother they refused. A nation once identified by strength ends identified by a messenger and a refusal.

phrases.translation: And to the people of Thamûd We sent their brother Ṣâliḥ.
phrases.explanation: To Thamud their brother Salih brings the pattern to a people remembered for carving homes in rock. Brother again means the warner grows from their own social soil rather than arriving as an unknown invader. The setting changes from Ad open strength to Thamud stone security, yet the first prophetic sentence will not change. Each civilisation receives a mirror fitted to the confidence it mistakes for permanence.

phrases.translation: He said, “O my people! Worship Allah. You have no god other than Him.
phrases.explanation: Worship Allah, no god other than Him, refuses to let technical skill become a theology. A people able to cut houses from mountains may feel unusually independent of weather, enemies, and time. Salih begins with the One who stands behind every tool and cliff. The sameness of the call across nations is part of its evidence, because different prophets are not marketing local preferences.

phrases.translation: He ˹is the One Who˺ produced you from the earth and settled you on it.
phrases.explanation: He produced you from the earth and settled you in it makes agriculture, building, and civilisation a divine permission. The word settled can carry cultivating and inhabiting through generations, a suitable dignity for people who engineered a landscape. Their hands truly carved stone, yet hands, stone, and life span all arrived from the earth Maker. Gratitude begins by placing achievement inside origin rather than letting origin be buried under achievement.

phrases.translation: So seek His forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance.
phrases.explanation: Seek forgiveness and repent uses the founding invitation for a people whose security might make guilt feel unnecessary. Repentance does not require a civilisation to hate its own houses or skills. It requires returning their meaning to the Giver and abandoning gods placed inside them. A carved home can become a place of worship or a small fortress against heaven depending on the loyalty of the family at the door.

phrases.translation: Surely my Lord is Ever Near, All-Responsive ˹to prayers˺.”
phrases.explanation: My Lord is Near and Responsive gives repentance an emotionally close destination. Nearness corrects the idea that a distant God must be approached through layers of invented beings, while Responsive promises that a returning voice is heard. For a people surrounded by stone walls, the image of a near Lord enters every room. Salih ends the invitation not with threat but with accessibility, making later refusal harder to blame on heaven remoteness.

phrases.translation: They argued, “O Ṣâliḥ! We truly had high hopes in you before this.
phrases.explanation: You were among us a person of hope before this reveals Salih earlier reputation for promise and good character. The council remembers liking him until his message touched ancestral worship. Social hope often means a rising person is expected to protect the group story well. Their surprise contains evidence in his favour, because only a sincere call could make a favoured young leader risk becoming unpopular in his own town.

phrases.translation: How dare you forbid us to worship what our forefathers had worshipped?
phrases.explanation: Do you forbid us to worship what our fathers worshipped makes ancestry the content of the objection. The question is less about defending the gods nature than defending continuity with dead parents and public memory. A son can feel that changing religion betrays a household table. Salih audience therefore argues from grief and belonging, powerful motives that the verse exposes without pretending they amount to proof.

phrases.translation: We are certainly in alarming doubt about what you are inviting us to.”
phrases.explanation: We are in disquieting doubt about what you call us to describes an inner disturbance they do not enjoy. The doubt is suspicious rather than open, agitating them because Salih known character will not let the message be dismissed as fraud. This is an important middle state between belief and settled denial. Discomfort could become inquiry if ancestry loosened its grip, or it could harden into the violence that follows.

phrases.translation: He responded, “O my people! Consider if I stand on a clear proof from my Lord and He has blessed me with a mercy from Him.
phrases.explanation: Consider if I am on clear proof and granted mercy repeats Noah argumentative shape for a new people. Salih asks Thamud to test his position rather than his popularity before the message disturbed them. Mercy from Allah likely means prophethood and its accompanying guidance, a gift he cannot return to the store because customers dislike it. The question invites them inside his dilemma without making their approval the measure of his duty.

phrases.translation: Who could help me against Allah if I were to disobey Him?
phrases.explanation: Who would help me against Allah if I disobeyed Him tells the council that yielding to them would not be a safe social compromise. Ancestors, chiefs, carved houses, and public hope cannot stand between a prophet and his Lord at judgment. The audience is asking him to purchase belonging at the highest possible price. His refusal therefore reads less as stubbornness and more as an accurate estimate of the court that matters.

phrases.translation: You would only contribute to my doom
phrases.explanation: You would only increase me in loss completes the exchange by pricing their offer. Keeping status among Thamud while disobeying revelation would empty his account with Allah. Loss language has travelled across the chapter from worldly seekers to this intimate temptation. Salih shows that even a prophet reputation can be spent badly if the applause of his people becomes more attractive than obedience.

phrases.translation: And O my people! This she-camel of Allah is a sign for you.
phrases.explanation: This she camel of Allah is presented as a sign with a simple public test attached. In the wider story she emerges in response to their demand and has an appointed share of water. Calling her Allah camel makes harm against her an offence against the sign Giver, not a dispute over livestock ownership. A visible creature drinking in public becomes a daily examination of whether Thamud can honour a limit.

phrases.translation: So leave her to graze ˹freely˺ on Allah’s earth and do her no harm, or a swift punishment will overtake you!”
phrases.explanation: Leave her to eat on Allah earth and do not touch her with harm gives repentance a very concrete form. Earth belongs to God, so the camel grazing is not stealing the tribe future. Near punishment is announced before the crime, removing surprise from the consequence. The whole nation is not asked first for a complex theology exam. They are asked to let one protected animal live.

phrases.translation: But they killed her, so he warned ˹them˺, “You have ˹only˺ three ˹more˺ days to enjoy life in your homes—this is an unfailing promise!”
phrases.explanation: They hamstrung her turns a chosen group act of defiance into the national turning point, since leaders and public consent surround the killing in the wider account. Three days of enjoyment in their homes gives a short calendar to people who trusted stone houses. A promise not to be belied settles the timing they previously used as mockery. The nearness makes each remaining ordinary hour morally loud.

phrases.translation: When Our command came, We saved Ṣâliḥ and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us and spared them the disgrace of that Day.
phrases.explanation: When Our command came Salih and believers were saved by mercy and from disgrace of that Day. Disgrace belongs to exposure as well as destruction, because a proud people end seen in the weakness they denied. Mercy again names survival as gift rather than superior engineering. The believers may have lived among the same rocks, yet allegiance rather than architecture determined which household had a future after the blast.

phrases.translation: Surely your Lord ˹alone˺ is the All-Powerful, Almighty
phrases.explanation: Your Lord is Strong and Mighty closes Thamud story with an answer to carved security. Strength in Allah does not need a quarry, scaffold, or mountain to prove it. Mighty conveys irresistible honour, the opposite of disgrace just mentioned. Two short names therefore carry the whole comparison between human works cut into cliffs and a power that can end a civilisation inside its most trusted rooms.

phrases.translation: And the ˹mighty˺ blast overtook the wrongdoers, so they fell lifeless in their homes
phrases.explanation: A mighty blast or shout seized the wrongdoers and morning found them fallen lifeless in their homes. Early commentators described a sound of overwhelming force, sometimes joined in broader accounts with earthquake. The details of mechanism can be held modestly, because the image of secure houses containing motionless bodies performs the moral work. A fortress becomes a tomb without needing its walls to fall first.

phrases.translation: as if they had never lived there. Surely Thamûd denied their Lord, so away with Thamûd
phrases.explanation: As if they had never lived in prosperity there measures how quickly noise, markets, children, smoke, and carved thresholds can become an uninhabited exhibit. A civilisation can leave impressive rooms and an empty social world at the same time. Surely Thamud disbelieved and away with Thamud sounds the same judgment formula heard after Noah and Ad. The verse asks later travellers to read absence as a sentence.

phrases.translation: And surely Our messenger-angels came to Abraham with good news ˹of a son˺.
phrases.explanation: Messenger angels come to Abraham with good news before the story turns toward Lot, linking birth and judgment inside one visit. Calling them messengers rather than simply guests announces their rank to the reader while Abraham still receives them as travellers. Good news in this setting will concern a son in old age. The scene begins with heaven bringing life into a house while carrying an errand of death toward a city.

phrases.translation: They greeted ˹him with˺, “Peace!” And he replied, “Peace ˹be upon you˺!”
phrases.explanation: Peace exchanged on both sides gives the meeting a courtesy that Abraham household will extend before identities are known.
